title: Fannkuch-redux
summary: Count pancake flips over all permutations of nine elements.
description: Classic Computer Language Benchmarks Game workload: for every permutation of 0..8 (generated in a fixed order) repeatedly reverse the first k+1 elements, where k is the first element, until the first element is 0. Prints an alternating-sign checksum of the flip counts and the maximum number of flips.
pseudocode:
perm1 = [0, 1, ..., n-1]; count = array of n zeros
for each permutation p of perm1 (fixed generation order):
    flips = 0; q = copy of p
    while q[0] != 0:
        reverse q[0..q[0]]                 # prefix of length q[0] + 1
        flips += 1
    maxflips = max(maxflips, flips)
    checksum += flips if permutation index is even else -flips
print checksum, maxflips
reveals: Tight loops over small integer arrays: indexing cost, bounds checks and branch prediction, with no allocation.
caveat: Single-threaded reference algorithm (no per-core splitting of the permutation space). Dominated by small array reads and writes, so interpreters are slowest by a large factor.
